title: Acoustics
description:
Coursework from MUSC 1325: Acoustics, spring 2026. Two projects: a gobo built in the scene shop, and a treatment plan for the home studio in my apartment office.

The studio is a 7'9" x 9'8" x 8' room. I measured it, calculated its room modes and RT60, modeled it in SketchUp, and designed a DIY fix. I was renting and on a budget, so the plan sticks to reasonable suggestions: Owens Corning 703 fiberglass panels and corner bass traps I could build myself. Untreated, the mids ring for over a second. With treatment, every band lands inside my 0.2 to 0.5 second target.

sections.label: Gobo
sections.desc: A gobo is a portable absorber, a go-between that can be moved around a room to control reflections. I built this one in the scene shop with a wood frame, fiberglass absorption, and a fabric cover.

images.alt: Finished gobo: a 2 by 4 foot wooden frame covered in grey fabric

sections.label: Room modes
sections.desc: Axial modes for the studio and the gap to the next mode up. The pairs at 70.6 / 72.9 Hz and 291.6 / 292.2 Hz stack almost on top of each other, which is why the low end needed attention.

sections.label: RT60
sections.desc: Reverb time before and after treatment, calculated from the room's surfaces and the added absorption. The target was 0.2 to 0.5 seconds in every band.

images.alt: Chart of RT60 by frequency: untreated peaks at 1.1 seconds near 500 Hz, treated stays at or under the 0.5 second target
images.caption: RT60 untreated, treated, and target

sections.label: Treatment plan
sections.desc: Six 2' x 4' panels (48 sq ft) of 703 fiberglass in plywood frames: two behind the monitors and two on each side wall at the first reflection points. Triangular DIY bass traps go in the corners that have room. A rug already covers most of the floor, and the wall behind the listening position is all doors, so there is no room for diffusion.
